outcome: Maternal composite outcome (post-partum hemorrhage, hemoglobin drop >= 4 gr/dL, blood transfusions, retained placental products, obstetric anal sphincter injuries)
cohort: The study included 332 parturients with known congenital uterine anomalies who had vaginal deliveries at a single tertiary center between 2005 and 2019.
finding: Vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD) in parturients with congenital uterine anomalies was independently associated with a significantly higher maternal composite outcome and increased rates of scalp trauma and Erb's palsy/clavicular fracture compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery (SVD).
mod_finding: Vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD) was associated with significantly higher rates of adverse maternal outcomes and perinatal birth trauma compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery (SVD).
